newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER SAYS K-SHAREHOLDERS IN TALKS TO SELL.
newsitem.headline: AMER SAYS K-SHAREHOLDERS IN TALKS TO SELL.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Monday it requested a share suspension on the Helsinki bourse because its vote-strong K-shareholders were in talks about selling their shares.
Amer said in a statement the K-shareholders, four domestic institutions, were negotiating with third parties about selling their shares. It did not elaborate on the talks.

It said it had requested the suspension of its shares until an extraordinary general meeting today on a proposed conversion of the unlisted K shares into listed A shares had been held. The meeting is due to start at 1400/1100 GMT.
The conversion has been seen by analysts as an opportunity for the K-shareholders to sell.
Amer's board is proposing to implement the conversion by redeeming all K-shares at a ratio of 1.2 A-shares for each K-share.
After the conversion, "Amer will have only one publicly listed share series, and all shares will carry equal voting rights," it said in a statement on May 6.
The company's four big K-shareholders had undertaken to subscribe A-shares of an equivalent value to their current holdings under a private placement, it said.

The entire K series is held by the company's four founding shareholders: the Finnish Association of Graduate Engineers, the Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration, the Finnish Association of Graduates in Economics and Business Administration, and the Land and Water Technology Foundation.
About a year ago, the K-shareholders said they had been approached by a potential buyer, but no deal ever took place.
